text: A class is a blueprint for creating your own custom type of object, bundling data and behavior together.
The dunder-init method is the constructor — it runs automatically when you create a new object.
self refers to the specific object being built, and we attach data to it, like name and age.
[chuckle] Methods are just functions defined inside the class — bark uses self to reach the object's own name.
To make an actual object, you call the class like a function, passing the values init expects.
Now Rex is a Dog object, and we can read its attributes with dot notation.
[sniff] Calling the bark method runs its code using this particular dog's data.
Every object you create is completely independent — Bella has her own name and age, separate from Rex.
[groan] Classes are how you model real things in code — a Dog, a User, an Order — each with its own state and actions.
In the next one we take on instance attributes. Follow so you don't miss it.
